projects.name: Dispatch Engine Simulator
projects.description: A real-time dispatch engine for delivery-style matching. It finds nearby drivers with Redis GEO lookups and a PostGIS fallback, scores and assigns them, retries failed dispatches through state machines, and publishes every state change to Kafka.
highlights: 5K-request bursty load test: about 180ms p95 dispatch latency and 92% dispatch success.
Shipped as freelance work for a food catering business: handles 300 orders/day and cut delivery-status inquiries by 90%.
Driver and order transitions are validated in the domain layer, so an invalid transition never reaches persistence.

projects.name: TinyLSM
projects.description: An LSM-tree key/value store in C++17 with a memtable, write-ahead log, SSTables with bloom filters and sparse indexes, and background leveled compaction. It is small enough to read in one sitting.
highlights: Demo writes 200k keys in 1,553 ms and reads back 50,000 of 50,000 random keys.
Crash recovery replays the WAL and scans SSTables on reopen, recovering all 50,000 sampled keys.
Background thread merges L0 into L1 and cascades levels as they exceed their byte budget.

projects.name: University Advisor Chatbot
projects.description: An agentic chatbot that gives international students source-cited university recommendations. It orchestrates Claude Sonnet through a tool-calling loop across 5 custom tools on a FastAPI backend, with a Next.js chat UI.
highlights: Sold and integrated into an Indian study-abroad consultancy's web app serving 500+ students weekly.
Tool-calling loop across 5 custom tools, with every recommendation citing its sources.

projects.name: locksmith
projects.description: A migration linter that predicts which PostgreSQL lock a DDL statement takes, whether it blocks reads or writes on the target server version, and roughly how long it holds the lock on a table of a given size.
highlights: Classifies statements into 18 operation kinds against the lock conflict matrix for PG 10, 11 and 12+.
Demo: a 400M-row table on PG 10 shows a 50.0 min write block, versus 5 ms on PG 16.
Suggests safe rewrites and treats unrecognised statements as worst case.

projects.name: sysprobe
projects.description: An eBPF profiler for Linux that records per-process syscall, run-queue and TCP connect latency. It exports Prometheus histograms and a top-style terminal view, with record and replay for offline analysis.
highlights: Kernel-side per-CPU log2 histograms, with every dropped sample counted and exported.
Verified end to end on two kernels: Linux 7.0.14-linuxkit (aarch64) and Linux 7.0.0-1017-azure (x86_64).
Replay runs the same aggregation and exporter offline, without privileges.

projects.name: gridboard
projects.description: A backpressure-aware telemetry buffer for grid dispatch consoles. Under overload it downsamples visibly, always keeps the newest sample, and marks panels STALE instead of showing old data as live.
highlights: Under 10x overload the bounded buffer detected 4/4 injected faults; an unbounded queue detected 0/4 with 18,001 samples backed up.
Seeded fault simulator and measurement harness; 16 tests.

projects.name: consentgraph
projects.description: Identity resolution where per-purpose consent gates the graph join itself. Match quality is measured as precision against planted ground truth, plus a household-confusion count.
highlights: Marketing purposes hold precision 1.0000 with 0 household confusions on 1,432 records and 472 real people.
Purpose-scoped traversal uses a recursive CTE over SQLite; consent is an append-only ledger.

projects.name: schemadrift
projects.description: A GraphQL breaking-change gate that downgrades severity using real field-usage telemetry. It names the client that still calls a removed field and posts a Markdown report suitable for a pull request.
highlights: Only removals of deprecated fields with zero callers in the window become SAFE; every downgrade is recorded with its justification.
Dependency-free SDL parser and structural diff.

projects.name: dmarcwatch
projects.description: Deliverability monitoring from DMARC aggregate reports. It parses RUA XML from five provider dialects, separates mail that never arrived from mail that arrived and was ignored, and flags unauthorised senders.
highlights: On a seeded corpus of 520,302 messages it found the planted break day, 2026-03-10, with DMARC pass rate falling from 100.0% to 15.0%.
Names the root cause of alignment failures instead of a bare DMARC fail.
